supported_claims.text: 下 is analyzed as an indicative graph: an early short mark below a longer reference line indicates “below.” The long line is interpreted either as a reference line or as the horizon.

In later forms the graph gained a descending vertical stroke, reportedly to distinguish it from 上 and 二. Accounts differ on whether this change was established in late Spring and Autumn forms or in small seal script.

Early oracle-bone examples show 下 used in references to lower deities and ancestral spirits; a cited bronze example uses it for the human world below. These examples attest uses but do not establish a complete semantic chronology.
Later cited uses include humility toward a superior, the verb “descend,” and “capture/take” in a military context. The dossier does not date a complete sequence connecting these uses.

The received Shuowen entry glosses 丅 as “bottom” and analyzes it as indicative, while identifying 下 as its seal-script form. This is a transmitted lexicographic analysis, not direct confirmation of the Shang graph’s shape or date.

disagreements.text: The graphic accounts differ over what the longer upper line represents: a general reference line or specifically the horizon.
The accounts place the distinguishing vertical stroke in different periods: late Spring and Autumn forms versus small seal script.

The dossier reports competing Proto-Sino-Tibetan and Austroasiatic proposals for the spoken word’s etymology, but neither proposal was independently verified in this research. They do not determine the graph’s formation.

limitations.text: No component split or phonetic element is supported by the inspected graphic analyses; 下 is explained as a whole indicative graph. The cited historical pronunciations concern 下 itself and do not establish a component reading.

The cited inscription examples and semantic uses were not independently checked against artifact photographs or dated editions; the evidence does not establish a complete dated sequence of meaning changes.
No specific dated specimen is supplied to settle when the lower mark changed to a vertical stroke. The curated seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.
